desc: The Mahābodhi Mahāvihāra marks the spot where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree. Originally built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BC, it has undergone several restorations over time. Its distinctive brick structure is one of the earliest examples of Buddhist temple architecture in India.
entities.name: Bodh Gayā

desc: The Great Pyramid of Cholollan was built in successive stages during hundreds of years. Dedicated to the deity Quetzalcōātl, it is the largest pyramid in the region. Even after the city's decline, it remained a sacred and cultural site for local inhabitants.
entities.name: Cholollan Holy City

desc: Founded in 788 AD on Mount Hiei by the monk Saichō, Enryaku-ji became the headquarters of the Tendai school of Japanese Buddhism. It was a powerful monastic center that housed thousands of warrior monks and influenced the affairs of Kyōto.
entities.name: Enryaku-ji

desc: Built in the 4th century under Emperor Constantine, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem encompasses both Golgotha and the tomb of Christ. It became the holiest site in Christianity and its most important pilgrimage center. Despite periods of destruction and reconstruction, it has remained in shared Christian custody.
entities.name: The Holy City of Jerusalem

desc: Located in Mecca and most commonly known as al-Ka'ba, the Al-Masjid al-Ḥarām is the most sacred shrine of Islam. Covered by a black cloth known as Kiswah, it defines the direction of prayer (qibla) for all Muslim prayers.
entities.name: Al-Masjid al-Ḥarām

desc: The Ranganathaswamy Temple in Srirangam is one of the largest and holiest Hindu temple complexes in India. Dedicated to the god Viṣṇu as Ranganatha, it dates at least from the early Chola period, with later extensions by the Pandya and Vijayanagara rulers. By 1337, it is a major pilgrimage center in Southern India, known for its vast precincts, imposing gopurams, and rich religious endowment.
entities.name: Ranganathaswamy Temple

desc: The Temple of Confucius in Qūfù, was originally built in 478 BC to honor the philosopher Confucius. Expanded repeatedly during successive dynasties, it became one of the largest temple complexes in China.
entities.name: Temple of Confucius

desc: The original Papal Basilica of Saint Peter in the Vatican in Rome was commissioned by Emperor Constantine in the 4th century over the tomb of Saint Peter, the first Pope. It became the principal church of Western Christianity and the seat of papal authority. It also is one of the main centers of pilgrimage for Catholicism.
entities.name: Saint Peter in the Vatican
